title: LRU cache with time-to-live
spec:
The repository is empty. Create `cache.py` with `class TTLCache(capacity, ttl, clock=time.monotonic)`.

- `capacity` must be an int >= 1 and `ttl` a number > 0, otherwise `ValueError`.
- `put(key, value)`: stores the value and records its put time `clock()`. Putting an existing key replaces its value, resets its put time, and makes it most recently used; it never evicts anything.
- An entry is expired when `clock() - put_time >= ttl`. Expired entries behave as absent everywhere.
- `get(key, default=None)`: returns the value (and makes the entry most recently used) or `default` when absent/expired. `get` does NOT extend the entry's lifetime.
- `key in cache` reports presence of a non-expired entry and does NOT change recency.
- `len(cache)` counts non-expired entries.
- Putting a NEW key into a cache holding `capacity` entries first discards all expired entries; only if it is still full is the least recently used entry evicted.

Inject `clock` in your tests instead of sleeping. Add unit tests runnable with `python3 -m unittest -q`.
acceptance: expiry, recency and eviction rules exactly as specified
expired entries are discarded before any live entry is evicted
